turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): sorry the wait ran long. i'm just getting vitals before dr. okonkwo comes in, arm straight please.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): yeah well i've been sitting out there forever and i didn't even want to come. just do it.
[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): blood pressure is one twenty-eight over eighty-two. pulse is 76.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm. fine.
[SEG0005] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): med list says diciclomine ten milligrams three times a day. you still on that?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): uh no. ten did nothing, i take twenty. three times a day, yeah, but twenty not ten.
[SEG0007] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): okay, i'll flag the dose. she should be right in.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): hi, i'm dr. okonkwo. sounds like a long morning. what brought you in today?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): these cramps, and my bowels are all over the place. i'm exhausted.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): okay. how long has it been, and what are the stools actually doing?

[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): a year. maybe a bit more, but basically a year. cramps come on and if i pass stool they ease off, and i'm bloated like six months pregnant by the afternoon, which i'm not. and it flips, constipated one day, loose and urgent the next, sorry.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): no apology needed. so cramps that ease after a bowel movement, bloating, and the habit swinging between constipation and loose stool, for a year. did i get that?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): yeah. that's it. and work is making me crazy on top.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): any blood in the stool, on the paper or mixed in?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): no. i looked. there's no blood.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): and weight, have you lost any without trying?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): no. i wish. if anything my pants are tight from the bloat. can we skip the twenty questions, i'm wiped.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): i'll keep it short. how often do the cramps hit, anything set them off?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): most days. worse when a deadline's on fire, and after lunch. um, nights are okay once i've gone.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): any family stuff, bowel disease, diabetes, blood pressure?

[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, my sister has pressure but no sugar. she's on biotin for her hair, that's hers. and my husband takes metformin for his diabetes, don't put that on my list.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): understood, none of those medicines are yours. what about work, and the day to day, food, exercise, drinking?

[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): i'm a project coordinator at a freight company, and the hours are brutal, like 55, sixty hours most weeks. diet is mostly a desk salad if i remember and takeout at nine. exercise, ha, i walk from the parking garage and that's it. alcohol, a glass of wine maybe two nights a week, not more, and i don't smoke, never did.

[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): project coordinator, 55 to 60 hours, salad if you remember otherwise late takeout, walking just from the garage, wine a couple of nights, never smoked. and the gut picture we said, a year, better after stool, no blood, no weight loss.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): yeah. don't get on me about the wine, it's not the problem.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): i'm not. alright if i feel your abdomen?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): fine. don't jab though, it hurts.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): soft. tender over the left lower side, no guarding, no masses that i can feel.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): see. told you.

[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): that pattern, the cramp easing when you pass stool, the bloating, constipation trading off with loose stool, fits a working impression of irritable bowel. i'm not calling it final until the labs are back.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): i'm ordering bloodwork today, a blood count, a crp, and a celiac panel. they can draw it before you go.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): more needles. great. will that even explain why i'm this tired?
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): it can pick up anemia or inflammation if one of those is sitting there. it won't measure the work stress, but it keeps us from missing something else.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): yeah the work stress isn't in a test tube. i know. i'm just tired of all of it.

[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): right. for food, smaller meals when you can, don't save the whole day of eating for nine o'clock, add some fiber like oats on the constipated days, and cut back on the greasy takeout. that's advice, not a speech.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): oats. sure. if i remember.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): i want to see you back in four weeks with the results. if the cramps or the stools get a lot worse before then, call the office.
[SEG0038] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): i can walk you to the lab for the blood draw now.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): err, yeah let's just get it over with.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): we'll go through the numbers together when you're back.

spec.situation: Person with cramps relieved by passing stool, bloating, alternating constipation and loose stools for a year; stress at work; denies blood and weight loss after prompting; bloods planned, diet advice.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

features: third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.
disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.

bad.reason: Husband's diabetes is mentioned, but not as family history in this extraction schema.
Bloating is supported, but transcript gives no clear 1-year duration for bloating specifically.
bad.text: Bloating (category=gastrointestinal, status=present, duration=1 year, temporality=current, body_site=abdomen, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

omissions.text: Recorded family history incorrectly includes husband with diabetes; the patient explicitly said her husband takes metformin for his diabetes and that this should not be put on her list, and the doctor confirmed those medicines/conditions were not hers.
Current dicyclomine dose is 20 mg three times a day; patient said 10 mg did nothing and she is taking 20 mg, not 10 mg.
Loose stools are described as urgent on the alternating days.
Symptoms are better at night once she has had a bowel movement ('nights are okay once I've gone').
Bloating worsens by the afternoon ('bloated like six months pregnant by the afternoon').
Family history negative for mother having diabetes ('mother did not').
